38b5bf31befbda5484188ef18734eb55bc559365.summary: Vulnerability research report on Cloak & Dagger, a class of Android attacks by Yanick Fratantonio, Chenxiong Qian, Simon Pak Chung and Wenke Lee. The attacks abuse two permissions, 'draw on top' and the accessibility service, to take control of the UI feedback loop. They include clickjacking, keystroke recording, security PIN stealing, phone unlocking with the screen off, and silent installation of a god-mode app. The report says the attacks affected Android 5.1.1, 6.0.1 and 7.1.2 as of June 2017 and were still practical. It also says Google marked several reports as won't fix or intended…

hedges: Most of these attacks are due to design issues, and they are thus challenging to prevent.
Previous versions are very likely to be vulnerable as well.
certain versions of Android may show "no permission required" even if, in fact, the app has access to both the permissions required for our attack.
